articleTitle: Minimal Peak Sidelobe Phase Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A new method of synthesis of code sequences for binary phase manipulation is proposed. One of the phase angles was optimized by solving the system of nonlinear equations. New code sequences were synthesized, and new phase sequences were constructed on their basis, which ensure the minimum level of the side lobes of the autocorrelation function. The results of the statistical analysis are given and the detection characteristics are calculated. The practical novelty of obtained results is in the expansion of the set of Barker code sequences.

articleTitle: Molecular Dynamics Study Of The Interface Amorphization In Ni/Ti Bi-Layered System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this work, the computer simulation using molecular dynamics approach was employed to study the initial stages of the diffusion and interfacial amorphization in the Ni/Ti bi-layer system. The processes of the diffusion-controlled growth of the amorphous phase were considered under different temperatures, heating rates, crystallographic orientations of the interacting metals, and presence or absence of the free surface. While the diffusion in the simulated system was frozen below 600 K, at higher temperatures it induced the formation of the amorphous phase at the interface. The amorphization process could be divided into three stages characterized by the different diffusivities. The probability of the growth of amorphous phase was higher for higher heating rates which is most likely associated with the interfacial stresses that had less time for relaxation. The presence of the free surface promoted the relaxation of the stresses along the direction perpendicular to the surface which was accompanied by the larger mean square atomic displacements of Ni and Ti, increasing the probability of the amorphous phase formation.

articleTitle: Passivating Oxide Layers on the Surface of InP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This study investigates the formation and characteristics of intrinsic oxide layers on the surface of n-type indium phosphide (InP), formed via electrochemical processing in a sulfuric acid environment. We have explored the oxide film's structure, chemical composition, and electronic properties using various analytical methods. The results indicate the formation of composite oxides with crackled morphologies and their impact on surface passivation. Our findings affirm the potential of InP native oxides for protective coatings yet highlight the need for further optimization to improve the uniformity and reduce the defectiveness of passivation layers.

articleTitle: Eigen Modes of the GTEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper addresses problems of TEM cell design used for wireless communication terminals testing with focus on GigaHertz TEM (GTEM) cells. To maximize usable test volume modern TEM cells often have an asymmetric design, where septum is displaced away from loading door of the cell. Doing so will alter electromagnetic field distribution, so quantitative characterization of this effect is required. The paper presents electromagnetic field problem solution for the eigenmodes of a cross-section of a TEM cell as a rectangular coaxial line. Dependencies of the electromagnetic field distribution and the characteristic impedance of the TEM mode on the geometrical parameters of the coaxial line have been obtained. They allow evaluation of the field inhomogeneity effect on the transmission coefficient from the input of the TEM cell to the antenna of the wireless communication device and facilitate matching impedance characteristics of the TEM cell with the input port. Though the usable space of the TEM cell with displaced septum is larger, maintaining nominal characteristic impedance along the cell cannot be achieved with simple trapezoid septum. Field uniformity in wider area degrades as well, which would require special measures to compensate this effect. Knowledge of the cutoff frequencies and distribution of the electromagnetic field of higher modes makes it possible to apply technical measures to improve the frequency characteristics of the transmission coefficient of the TEM cell by reducing the influence of higher modes on the general structure of the field along the direction of propagation of electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: The Effect of Thermal Annealing on the Crystal Structure and Surface Morphology of Spincoated P(VDF-TrFE) Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: P(VDF-TrFE) copolymer has attracted great attention of researchers due to its ferro-, piezo-, and pyroelectrical properties combined with mechanical flexibility, biocompatibility, easy manufacturing, high chemical resistance, and other advantages. This can be promising for a variety of applications such as fabrication of sensors, actuators, wearable electronics, green energy devices. This material can exist in non-polar (alpha) and polar (beta, gamma) molecular conformations. A beta-phase is the most interesting in terms of ferroelectricity. The common approach for preparation P(VDF-TrFE) with enhanced beta-phase content is annealing the polymer at typical temperatures of above 140 Celsius degrees after its formation. The authors demonstrate (and confirm another similar reports) that at certain conditions P(VDF-TrFE) can directly crystallize into beta-conformation from a solution during its spincoating. This is confirmed by the methods of IR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction for thin films (about 200 nm) prepared by spincoating solutions of P(VDF - TrFE) (75:25 molecular composition) in dimethylacetamide. The techniques and characterization described in the paper can be of some practical interest for polymer ferroelectric films fabrication.

articleTitle: Electron- Phonon Interaction in Open GaAs/AIAs Nanosystems: A New Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A new theoretical method for describing electron-phonon interaction in open nanosystems created on the basis of gallium arsenide and aluminium arsenide alloys in the presence of a time-dependent electromagnetic field is proposed. The results obtained on the basis of the developed method are compared with the results obtained on the basis of the classical model of closed nanosystems. The conditions and configurations of the nanosystems under study for which the results of both methods coincide have been established by the direct calculations.

articleTitle: Threshold Conditions for 1-D Model of Solid State Laser with Fabry-Perot Resonator: Gain Medium Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The study considers the threshold conditions for a plane-parallel laser model containing a gain medium filled cavity, or a Fabry-Perot resonator, sandwiched between two distributed Bragg reflectors. We implemented the Lasing Eigenvalue Problem approach to study the mode-specific frequencies and the threshold gain index values. Within this approach, we look for these values as components of two-component eigenvalues of a specific boundary problem where the active region is taken into account ad characterized with the aid of imaginary part of the refractive index of the gain medium. This analysis can be used in the optimization of the laser performance as lower threshold is known to lead to larger output power in the real-life laser emission.

articleTitle: Dynamic Alterations in Internal Defect-Associated Free Volume within Ge-Ga-S(CsC1) Glass for Photonic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Dynamic alterations in internal defect-associated free volume in the Ge-Ga-S glasses with different amount of CsCl content were investigated using positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy. The presence of CsCl in the glassy matrix of Ge-Ga-S subjected to cold crystallization leads to a change in free volume defects, which are described by the parameters of the second component of the annihilation spectrum. It is shown that the addition of CsCl to the base glass results in the agglomeration of free volume defects, their increase, and further fragmentation in samples with the highest CsCl content. In the case of nanocomposites, where processes are described by the third component of the annihilation spectrum, initial pore agglomeration processes occur, followed by a decrease in their quantity and size with the addition of optimal CsCl content and an increase with maximum CsCl content as wel as addition annihilation in water. Analyzing the obtained results allows selecting samples with optimal CsCl content for further practical applications in photonics and sensing.

articleTitle: Model of Studying the Membrane Potential in the Interaction of Cell Structure with an Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Understanding the workings of the cellular system is a key element in the further development of this area of research. The functioning of the cellular system has a complex descriptive mathematical structure; a qualitative understanding of the life cycle is impossible without taking into account the role of the membrane potential and electrophysiological phenomena in the cells of multicellular organisms. Membrane potential plays a key role in the regulation of cellular metabolism and other cellular processes. In addition, the study indicates the possibility of correcting changes in cellular processes by influencing the membrane using electromagnetic fields. The development of models of the functioning of the cell membrane under the influence of an electric field can lead to a deeper understanding of the processes of disinfection and stimulation of biological processes in organisms. This can lead to complete randomization of cell vibrations, which reflects the influence of the magnetic field on cellular processes. Studies have shown that changing the characteristics of the external electromagnetic field allows you to effectively control the state and dynamics of the cell.

articleTitle: Development Features of Metrological Equipment for Monitoring the Growth of III- V Heterostructures using MOCVD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: For all types of MOCVD reactors for the growth of III-V structures there are common, but at the same time quite critical technical issues. Thereby, it is worth highlighting the large temperature gradients in the reactor, which lead to the formation of convection loops, the high-speed of the gas flow, which can lead to turbulence instead of the expected laminar flow, as well as the need for precise control of the temperature on the surface of the semiconductor wafer in the real time. To obtain high-quality heterostructures with reproducible parameters, it is important to have a system of precise temperature control on the wafer surface directly in the deposition area, since the deposition process for many complex semiconductor devices (for example, laser diodes, light-emitting diodes, photodetectors) is very sensitive to temperature changes. Moreover, as structures grow, the optical properties of their surface change, so the temperature monitoring system uses the emissivity-compensation pyrometry method to accurately determine the parameters and calculate the true temperature of the surface. This paper is devoted to the detailed analysis of the method of registration and formation of an optical signal in a pyrometer-reflectometer, determination of the optimal spectral range, investigation of the characteristics of detectors and emitters of the IR range. The purpose of the article is to determine the main technical criteria for the selection or development of active optoelectronic elements for a precision wafer temperature control system during the production of semiconductor heterostructures based on III- V solid solutions for micro-optoelectronics devices.

articleTitle: Development of Methods for Image Filtering in Noise and their Implementation for a Web Service
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Known image processing software systems use filtering methods such as the Gaussian filter, the median filter, and others, which often do not have satisfactory performance in processing certain types of noise. This leads to a partial loss of the useful signal and a deterioration in image quality. The work is devoted to improving the quality of image filtering in various kinds of noise. A model of additive interaction of signals in additive impulse noise is proposed. A new method of least finite differences (MLFD) for image filtering has been developed. An interactive web service for the implementation of MLFD was created. Various filtering methods have been proposed to reduce the effect of impulsive noise on images. The proposed data processing is based on a priori information about the type of noise. The web service is a flexible and efficient solution for filtering digital images and is not available in well-known graphics packages. The new web service is a good compromise between the quality of filtering and the simplicity of the solution compared to complex and resource-intensive systems for graphic image processing.

articleTitle: Simulation of Plasmonic Properties of Gold Nanoparticle Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper presents the results of modeling the plasmonic properties of gold nanoparticles array using numerical models built using the COMSOL Multiphysics software. Densely packed arrays of plasmonic nanoparticles exhibit extremely strong light-matter interaction via plasmonic coupling. A study of near-field interaction and changes in the absorption, scattering, and transmission parameters of Au nanoparticles arrays with a change in particle size in direct normal incidence of optical radiation was conducted. Individual near-field optical properties, as well as the mechanism of plasmon relaxation of nanoparticles, change with increasing nanoparticle size. The intensity and direction of the local field depends on the polarization, the angle of incidence and the wavelength of the incidence. In general, it is shown that arrays of plasmonic nanoparticles provide broadband absorption, reflectance, transmittance, and strong near-field enhancement.

articleTitle: Prototype Device for Measuring Carbon Monoxide Levels in Human Exhalation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The development of devices for a rapid, non-invasive, cost-effective real-time health monitoring process capable of assessing human environmental impact is a promising area of scientific research. This approach has enormous potential for non-invasive disease diagnosis. Analysis of the air exhaled by a person has long attracted the attention of developers and scientists in the field of medical diagnostics and disease monitoring. After all, volatile compounds present in exhalation are biomarkers of various diseases, and their increased concentrations indicate the progression of the disease. Therefore, breath analysis is a promising tool for early detection of diseases. But currently available devices are often bulky, slow and expensive. The purpose of our work is to create a device prototype for non-invasive monitoring of persons affected by carbon monoxide poisoning or smoke inhalation. This device is intended for use in mobile ambulances, fire and rescue operations and intensive care units.

articleTitle: Computer-Based Modeling of Field-Managed Percolation in 3D Arrangements of Linear Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The investigation focused on the phenomenon of percolation within a system of straight nanotubes, with the development of an adapted model to characterize this process. A computational algorithm was devised to ascertain the percolation probability of nanotubes, utilizing tools for 3D graphics visualization. The study delved into the impact of geometric dimensions and nanotube concentration on the percolation probability. The research explored the correlation between percolation probability and the dispersion angle, which determines the orientation of nanotubes. By analyzing this relationship, fundamental patterns emerged in the formation of conductive clusters under the influence of an electric field. This analysis facilitated the identification of optimal parameters for a nanotube system capable of demonstrating field-controlled percolation.

articleTitle: CubeSat Si Solar Cells Long-Term Degradation in Open-Space Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This study evaluates the enduring performance of silicon solar cells aboard the 2014-launched CubeSat, PolyITAN-1. Despite lower efficiency, cost-effectiveness and reliability were prioritized for the satellite's energy requirements. Ground tests indicated a 24 % efficiency and 7W capacity. In space, telemetry data revealed individual solar panel capacities of 1-1.5W, totaling 8-9W. High radiation levels in the inner Van Allen Belt caused cell degradation, aligning with modeling predictions of up to 70 % reduction in the first two years, stabilizing at 20–30 % thereafter. Contrary to predictions, some cells exhibited less than 10% degradation during first years, credited to advanced technology incorporating a back-surface field and reflector structure and high-carrier-lifetime silicon wafers. The PolyITAN-1 mission showcases CubeSats as cost-effective space access for education and research, with the chosen solar cells demonstrating remarkable resilience to open-space challenges.

articleTitle: 1D Silicon Nanostructures for Detection of Volatile Organic Compounds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this work, ethanol vapor diode sensors based on silicon nanowires (SiNWs) were fabricated. SiNWs were obtained by metal-assisted chemical etching technique (MACE). Surface morphology, electrical and gas sensitive characteristics were studied. It was determined the influence of MACE synthesis parameters on sensor efficiency. Also we showed the effect of presence of textured surface of the silicon wafer and additional processing of it in the isotropic/anisotropic etchants on the device characteristics. The obtained sensors are characterized by a rectification ratio of 1836 and a response value to the gas analyte (ethanol) of 25, which are 11 and 6 times higher than for a silicon sensor without SiNWs, respectively.

articleTitle: H-Polarized THz Wave Scattering by Dielectic Cylinder With Graphene Strip Inside It
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We consider the scattering of the H-polarized plane wave by a dielectric cylinder with single graphene strip placed symmetrically inside it in the THz frequency range. Hyper-singular integral equation relatively currents density on the strip is obtained, which is numerically solved with the Nystrom-type algorithm. The solution is meshless and full-wave. By varying the chemical potential, the radar cross-section of the considered configuration can either decrease or increase compared to that of the corresponding bare dielectric cylinder.

articleTitle: Spectral Properties of Quasiparticle Interacting With Three-Mode Phonons, Taking Into Account Damping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Within the model of quasiparticle in two states interacting with three-mode polarization phonons at T=0K, the Fourier image of the Green's function is calculated considering non-phonon scattering mechanisms, which are taken into account by phenomenological damping. Accurate analytical expressions are obtained for the stationary energy spectrum of such system and the shape-function of its absorption band. It made possible to analyze the spectral properties of the system with and without the non-phonon damping.

articleTitle: Biosensing Photonic Scheme on a Black Phosphorus DBR Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A photonic heterostructure based on the plane black phosphorus and a distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) for the detection of biological agents in the terahertz frequency range is considered. Based on a previously proposed scheme of a photonic device for control of terahertz radiation, a scheme of biosensor for environmental analysis is proposed. Modeling of the detection process was carried out by the transfer-matrix method. The influence of changing the parameters of the photonic device and the characteristics of detected biological agents on the spectral properties of the photonic device was studied for biological objects and can be used for classification tasks.

articleTitle: Non-orthogonal Configuration of MEMS Sensors Analysis Based on Allan Variance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper deals with the non-orthogonal configuration of MEMS inertial measuring units analysis based on Allan variance. The influence of changes in the measurement range of the InvenSense MPU6050 inertial module on the Allan variance was assessed. Based on an analysis of the results of the Allan variance assessment, a procedure for choosing multi-axis MEMS sensors with identical characteristics to create an inertial non-orthogonal measuring instrument is proposed. An example of compiling a data processing algorithm for an inertial measuring instrument with a non-orthogonal arrangement of sensitivity axes based on an assembly of 3-axis MEMS sensors is given. The simulation results for numerical estimates are represented. Improvement of the accuracy of the non-orthogonal inertial measuring instruments using the Allan variance is shown.

articleTitle: Performance Study of COFDM Designs in Coherent Detection Optical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The article studies the effectiveness of using OFDM-coded (COFDM - Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing) signal structures in optical channels with dispersion. An assessment of the noise immunity of optical channels with OFDM in the case of compensation for dispersion components is presented. The main contribution of the article is to consider the principles of using Low-density parity-check code (LDPC) codes for optical channels. The results of mathematical modeling of possible scenarios for the use of LDPC codes for optical coherent channels under dispersion conditions are analyzed. To determine the adequacy of the proposed solutions, circuit solutions for signal generation and processing are presented. The results obtained will be useful for the correct choice of channel multiplexing strategy in optical communications.

articleTitle: Hybrid System for Passive Location of Sound and Seismic Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of a joint system of sound location and seismic location for identifying air and ground moving objects using a distributed network of sensors. The main difference from existing passive location systems that use the TDOA method is the determination of the time delay by the cross-correlation function of signals from spaced sensors for stationary objects, and by the mutual uncertainty function for moving objects. There is also the computational complexity of processing wideband signals in the time, spectral and Doppler domains. If for stationary targets processing in the spectral-temporal domain based on the fast Fourier transform is sufficient, then for moving targets additional computational costs are required due to the need for multi-channel processing in the Doppler frequency domain. The purpose of the article is to study the potential capabilities of a hybrid system of sound and seismic location based on improving the layout of semi-natural modeling. The analysis of the effectiveness of integrating sound-location and seismic-location systems showed the potential capabilities of detecting, recognizing and determining the coordinates of unmanned aerial vehicles, as well as other moving and stationary objects with an accuracy sufficient for further tracking of targets by means of visual surveillance.

articleTitle: Finite Sparse Circular Dielectric Graphene-Wrapped Nanowire Grating Excited by Modulated Beam of Electrons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The infrared-range diffraction radiation from a finite grating made of circular graphene-wrapped dielectric nanowires excited by the beam of electrons is considered. The beam is density-modulated and its velocity is considered constant. The characterization of graphene involves the quantum-theory Kubo formalism and the boundary conditions of resistive sheet. In order to transform the electromagnetic wave scattering boundary value problem into a well-conditioned algebraic equation for the scattered field expansion coefficients, we use the separation of variables and the cylindrical functions addition theorem, plus analytical regularization. This guarantees the convergence and provides easy numerical accuracy control. The emphasis of this research is on the resonance effects associated to the plasmon and lattice modes. The applications potential of the numerical results is discussed.

articleTitle: Optical Control of Electron Population Density Distribution in Si:YIG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Perspective electronic devices for signal processing at microwave band may require having tunable parameters with possibility of easy and rapid control by external variables, like electric/magnetic fields, currents or electromagnetic wave. The latter can be created based on Si doped yttrium iron garnet material, which has optoinduced modification of electron populations density distribution caused by, among others, infrared beam irradiation. That phenomenon may be described by electron hopping model. Due to electron density redistribution the additional uniaxial magnetic anisotropy field appears, which allows to register in dynamics the changes in above-mentioned distribution by experimental investigation of ferromagnetic resonance frequency behavior of Si doped yttrium iron garnet samples, which strongly depends on its anisotropy fields. Theoretical model of resonance frequency shift is presented in this work. The influence of incident wave polarization and its intensity on electron distribution and, finally, on ferromagnetic resonance frequency was experimentally measured and discussed.

articleTitle: Modified Coplanar Vivaldi Antenna for Measuring Blood Glucose Concentration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Every year, three million people worldwide die from diabetes mellitus, which is the equivalent of one death every 10 seconds. There is a need for new technologies that provide reliable and continuous glucose measurements, while being unobtrusive for patients. Glucose monitoring is useful not only for diabetics but also for astronauts, athletes, and security personnel. This study proposes a new method for non-invasive blood glucose monitoring using a coplanar Vivaldi antenna as a microwave sensor. This antenna, operating at a frequency of 8 GHz, allows accurate measurements with a peak gain of 6.20 dBi. It was designed and simulated by ANSYS HFSS using Rogers RT/duroid 5880 material as the substrate with dielectric constant of 2.2.

articleTitle: P-I-N Photodiode with Optical Concentrator for the Near-IR Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The article considers the possibility of using an optical concentrator in the design of a photodiode with an adsorption filter to level the absorbed radiation by the light filter. A silicon p-i-n photodiode crystal with a guard ring isotypic to the substrate material was used as a photosensitive element. During the research, it was found that the photo signal when using the optical concentrator increases by 1.7 times (in the design used) relative to the signal on the responsive crystal when measured in the focused emitter mode, and by 2.5 times in the parallel flow mode. The parameters of the obtained photodiode were also compared with analogs available on the market. It was found that our proposed filter is the most selective of the compared options. It is also shown that the filters used in analogs do not shift the maximum spectral response. The obtained photodiodes can compete with PD with optical concentrators and light filters on the market and may even be the best among similar samples in capacitance, responsivity, half angle degree and other.

articleTitle: High-Selectivity Resonators Based on Transmission Line Sections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The high quality factor of a two-stub resonator is achieved due to the high steepness of the frequency dependence of the resonator reactive conductance. However, such a resonator does not provide high selectivity in the suppression band. In the presented paper, the structure of a basic unit formed by two transmission line sections is proposed, and resonators based on these units are considered. The high quality factor of such resonators is achieved due to the very low value of resonator active conductance. Resonators have a high selectivity in the suppression band. The transmission responses of various resonator variants are presented.

articleTitle: Modification of Optical and Dielectric Properties of Microcrystalline Cellulose by K2SO4 and K2Bi(PO4)(MoO4):Pr Complex Oxides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Cellulose materials are considered alternatives for artificial polymer usage in electronics. Nanosized inorganic and carbon additives can improve mechanical, electrical, optical, and other properties of micro/nanocrystalline cellulose and its derivatives. The set of nanocomposites based on microcrystalline cellulose and oxide compounds were produced in the form of tablets and have been characterized in this work by means of FTIR, luminescence spectroscopy and dielectric relaxation measurements. The influence of oxide additives on the luminescent and dielectric properties of nanocomposites has been analyzed.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of the Ensembles of the Spherical Nanoparticles, Embedded into the Thin-film Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The optical properties of the ensembles of mono- and bimetallic nanoparticles, which are used for the improvement of the technical characteristics of the thin-film solar cells, are studied in the article. The frequency dependencies of the radiation efficiency, absorption, scattering and reflection coefficients for the ensembles of mono-and bimetallic particles have been calculated. It has been established that for an ensemble of monometallic particles, the absorption and scattering coefficients are greater than in the case of an ensemble of bimetallic nanoparticles. The practical recommendations are presented regarding the size and morphology of nanoparticles, which are embedded in the solar cell, in terms of absorption enhancement or scattering.

Author Keywords: averaged absorption and scattering cross- sections

articleTitle: 3D Photoluminescence Response Pattern of Nanoparticle Sensor System as the “Artificial Taste” of Alcoholic Beverages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A novel and sensitive approach has been investigated for discerning similar alcoholic beverages, utilizing 3D analyte “taste” patterns derived from analyte photoluminescent responses in the presence of synthesized fluorinated carbon nanoparticles (FCNP). Fabrication of fluorescent FCNP was carried out by implementing a modified solvothermal synthesis followed by nanoparticle parameters monitoring using atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging and dynamic light scattering spectroscopy (DLS). The method of concentration-dependent photoluminescence was used to determine the optimal parameters of the colloidal solution of the FCNP-analyte sensor system to maximize the selectivity of the 3D patterns sensor response on analytes presence. The photoluminescence patterns of the colloidal solution of FCNP were obtained for similar production technology alcoholic beverages such as armagnac, cognac, and whiskey. The photoluminescence response pattern exhibited by the FCNP-based sensor system is distinctive for the analyzed analytes and the reference mixture of ethanol and water. The action of the aromatic molecules of a specific analyte forms a unique photoluminescent response pattern of FCNP that can be used for systems like “artificial tongue”. Principal component analysis (PCA) depicts clear clusters for beverage and references. The clusters corresponding to cognac and armagnac closely align with each other, illustrating the inherent affinity between these alcoholic beverages.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Technology of Discrimination of Dielectric Cylinders Using Multifrequency Reflectivity Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The possibility of estimating the diameter of dielectric cylinders using discrimination by the three-component stacked artificial neural network (ANN) in the microwave range is under consideration. The network consists of two sparse autoencoders and the softmax unit. The input dataset is formed from 2D reflectivity images in the coordinates of longitudinal sensing and transverse scanning. It is possible to synthesize a time signal along longitudinal axes from multi-frequency reflectivity measurements in frequency range of 38–52 GHz using an analytical signal approach, which allows one to obtain amplitude and phase distributions. The novelty of the research lies in the analysis the effect of using both amplitude and phase information for discrimination. For ANN training, 2D reflectivity distributions for cylinders with the radius of 15 to 35 mm are calculated using the method of auxiliary sources (MAS). The possibility of successful recognition was confirmed for the case of the diameter deviation of 1 mm and the presence of additive Gaussian noise with SNR of down to 0 dB.

articleTitle: Method for Sampling Narrowband Radio Signals with Known Center Frequency of Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: When processing radio signals, the volume of computational operations depends on the number of discrete samples during analog-to-digital conversion. We propose a method for significantly reducing such samples for the case of narrowband radar signals with a known center frequency. In this case, the narrowband is determined by the significantly smaller width of the spectrum of the received radar signal compared to the operating frequency of the intermediate frequency amplifier, from the output of which the signal is fed to an analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The main feature of the proposed procedure is that the sequence of ADC sampling clock pulses is organized in such a way that any two adjacent samples are related by a quadrature ratio. It is shown that this procedure makes it possible to determine the amplitude and phase of the received signal corresponding to each sample. At the same time, it remains possible to calculate the Doppler shift and signal envelope parameters. A computer simulation of the proposed sampling method was carried out at the repetition rate of the ADC sampling clock pulses, which is determined by the frequency of the reference signal of the master system of the coherent radar and is a multiple of the operating frequency of the intermediate-frequency amplifier. The relative error in determining the signal amplitude is formed as a result of the inequality in the frequencies of the received and reference signals. For real conditions, it does not exceed 1 % and depends on the characteristics of the radar (carrier frequency of the sounding signal, the multiplicity between the value of the intermediate frequency at which processing is carried out and the value of the sampling frequency), as well as on the value of the radial velocity of the object and the initial phase difference between the signal at the output of the intermediate-frequency amplifier and reference signal. The proposed method for converting narrowband radio signals into a digital format can significantly reduce the volume of operations performed and, accordingly, reduce time of processing both reflections from point-like objects (spacecraft, airplanes), and incoherent scatter signals from a distributed target. In some cases, this makes it possible to use the freed up time for computer processing of a large array of useful information in real time.

articleTitle: Method for the Automatic Modulation Classification for the Sums of Phase- Shift-Keying Signals Based on Polynomial Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper considers the task of automatic modulation classification for the sums of phase-shift keying (PSK) signals which occupy the same frequency bandwidth and have the same modulation. This problem is an important step which precedes the subsequent processing of such signals. For the solution of this classification problem we implement the method based on two machine learning tools: logistic regression or two-layer feedforward neural network. It allows to determine the class to which the sum of two PSK signals belongs. As the features used for the input of these classifications tools, we use second-order polynomial features calculated based on higher order cumulants of the received signal. The results of numerical experiments using different channel parameters and noise levels show the advantage of implementing second-order features over the raw features both in the case of logistic regression and two-layer feedforward neural network.

articleTitle: Atomic Force Microscopy Imaging and Fractal Analysis of Surface Roughness of Polyvinyl Alcohol-Chitosan Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-Chitosan films were studied by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), atomic force microscopy (AFM), ultrasonic force microscopy (UFM) and lateral force microscopy (LFM) and the results were compared to those of pure PVA and pure chitosan films. The surface of PVA-chitosan blends consists of small, rounded clusters, and random pores, but in contrast to the individual component films, inhomogeneous features were observed on the surface, in the form of relatively large higher clusters, which gave rise to lower elastic and frictional contrast. In addition, UFM and LFM revealed the presence of softer and lower friction regions which could not be distinguished in the topographic images. Such areas may be related to the formation of a new different phase as a result of PVA-chitosan interactions. TGA confirmed an increase in the thermal stability of the PVA-chitosan blend compared to the individual component films. The dependence of the root mean square (RMS) roughness on length scale was investigated. It was shown that the PVA-chitosan film has a higher RMS roughness for shorter measured lengths than the pure PVA samples, but the roughness for long measured lengths is lower than in pure PVA samples, which is explained by the lower Hurst number of the PVA-chitosan blend. The Hurst exponent and fractal dimension of the samples were obtained, which indicate a higher level of fractality and a more irregular shape of the surface topography for the PVA-chitosan films.

articleTitle: Transformation of Correlation Function Forms for Targets in a 94 GHz Noise Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This work is devoted to studying and clarifying the mechanism for transforming the shapes of the correlation function received from a target in a noise signal for a 3mm wavelength radar. The relevance of considering this issue is due to the fact that the features of such transformation observed in practice make it difficult to ensure the potential spatial resolution of closely located small objects or elements of spatially distributed targets, and also worsen the possibility of their identification. As a result of a comparison of experimentally obtained results with the results of theoretical modeling, it is shown that the shape of the correlation function in a noise radar with a given frequency response (FrR) of the receiving path significantly depends on the results of the phase addition of signals received from target elements located in the pulse volume of the radiation pattern (RP) spot. To study these features, the effectiveness of an approach based on the use of shaping filters is demonstrated and the possibility of adequately describing, using such a model, the processes of interaction of a noise pulse signal with various types of targets and hardware parameters of the radar is shown.

articleTitle: Strain-Polarization Coupling in the Low-Dimensional Van der Waals Ferrielectrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Using the Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire phenomenological approach we explore the strain-polarization coupling in the low-dimensional van der Waals ferrielectrics. We evolve the analytical model of the piezoelectric susceptibility of the material in response to the periodic strain modulation, such as caused by a surface acoustic wave. Numerical calculations are performed for recently discovered and poorly studied ultrathin layers of vdW ferrielectric CuInP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, which are very promising candidates for advanced nanoelectronics. We obtained that the temperature dependences of the dielectric and piezoelectric susceptibilities, and elastic compliance of the ultrathin CuInP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> layer have a sharp maximum at the temperature of CuInP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> paraelectric-ferrielectric phase transition near 320 K. The magnitudes of the dielectric and piezoelectric susceptibilities, and elastic compliance depend significantly on the modulation period of the surface acoustic wave. Obtained results explore the potential of ultrathin CuInP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> layers for application in piezoelectric and straintronic devices.

articleTitle: Abnormal Ideality Factor and LED Noise Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The investigation of the I- V characteristic and the ideality factor supplemented by the analysis of electrical and optical noise for different RGB and IR LEDs was conducted. It is shown that the typical dependence of ideality factor on current for the batches of green., blue., and red LEDs differs from an “abnormal” dependence obtained for some IR LEDs. Several samples of IR LEDs demonstrated sharp peaks in the ideality factor dependence at current values that differed from sample to sample from the same batch. The measurements of the noise characteristics at these currents revealed the strong correlations between ideality factor peaks' location and relevant electrical noise increase. This may indicate the appearance of a leakage current that fluctuates. At the same time., the current attributed to radiative recombination remains the same., which is confirmed by both the optical noise spectra and the radiation flux characteristics.

articleTitle: Step-by-step Evolution of Femtosecond Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures on Silicon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Consecutive stages of femtosecond laser treatment of crystalline silicon, aiming in laser-induced periodic surface structure (LIPSS) formation, have been explored by means of real-time optical emission spectroscopy and the following diffraction pattern imaging. Using of a cylindrical lens to focus laser radiation make it possible to process a large area by just one laser pulse. A clean surface, LIPSS without ablation, and a highly distorted surface could be obtained depending on the quantity of laser pulses applied.

articleTitle: Phase Stability of ZnSb-SnTe Thin Films with High Thermoelectric Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Thermoelectric materials are the basis of devices for the direct conversion of thermal energy into electrical energy, thereby creating a reliable prospect for the development of the energy industry. The wide possibilities of miniature devices, which have recently opened up in connection with the use of Internet of Things technology, urgently require flexible autonomous power sources. Therefore, the search for flexible thermoelectric materials with high figure of merit is currently an urgent task. The article theoretically studies the phase stability of thin films of pseudobinary semiconductor alloys ZnSb-SnTe. The obtained <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T-x$</tex> phase diagrams made it possible to predict the existence of a wide miscibility gap. Taking into account small internal stresses and the influence of the quartz substrate did not lead to significant changes in the phase diagram depending on the film thickness. It has been shown that spinodal decomposition processes caused by annealing at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T=225^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{ZnSb})_{1-\mathrm{X}}(\text{SnTe})_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> alloys at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x=0.27$</tex> lead to microstructural evolution with the formation of precipitates of the SnSb metal phase. This fact is in good agreement with the experimental studies of the thin films considered and is the reason for the sharp increase in the power factor to 3383 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{Wm}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$</tex> at 300°C. The described recrystallization processes are the main mechanism for the high thermoelectric characteristics of this material.

articleTitle: Silver Ellipsoidal Nanoparticles for Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The plasmon absorption cross-section spectra for spherical nanoparticles of silver, gold, and copper were calculated and studied. Silver nanoparticles are characterized by the highest intensity of absorption peak. The absorption spectra of ellipsoidal silver nanoparticles are considered in detail. Such nanoparticles demonstrate significant enhancement of the electric field at the ends of the ellipsoid and can be tuned by changing the shape. Change in the shape of nanoparticles from spherical to ellipsoidal in two different axes results in splitting the absorption spectrum of the silver nanoparticles into two separate peaks. It was shown that silver ellipsoidal nanoparticles are promising candidates for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy that can work at two different excitation wavelengths of 532 nm and 785 nm, correspondingly.

articleTitle: Energy Loss of a Charged Particle Moving in a Magnetic Field Along a Spiral Trajectory Around a Conducting Solid-State Plasma Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: An important characteristic of the possible process of generating electromagnetic waves is the energy loss of a moving charged particle per unit time by excitation of eigenwaves in the system. Using Maxwell's equations, the energy loss of a charged particle moving in an external magnetic field along a spiral trajectory around a conducting solid-state plasma cylinder have been found. The conditions under which magneto-bremsstrahlung radiation of electromagnetic waves occurs in the system have been formulated. The expression for the energy loss of a moving charge has been obtained. This expression has a universal character. With its help, it is possible to determine the energy loss of a particle both when the particle moves around the cylinder and when it moves translational parallel to the element of cylinder.

Author Keywords: energy loss of a particle by radiation

articleTitle: Effect of Substrate on Frequencies and Thresholds of the E- Polarized Modes of Microsize Graphene Strip Grating Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This mathematical model relating to E-polarized laser eigenmodes was considered. The laser system consists of an infinite grating of graphene strips placed on an active substrate specially made of gain material and is considered at the point of stationary light emission. Our model is firmly rooted within classical electromagnetics except the description of the graphene conductivity, which is borrowed from the quantum theory. The mode problem is reduced to two independent determinantal equations for the orthogonal symmetry classes. Our approach hinges on analytically inverting the static component of the problem related to the free-space grating, utilizing the Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (IDFT) technique. Consequently, the matrices underpinning these determinantal equations belong to the Fredholm condition of the second kind provides a mathematical verification of the convergence of truncated deterministic equations to the desired eigenvalues as the truncation order grows. Based on the developed algorithm, we computed the frequencies and thresholds related to different modes of laser emission of a microsize graphene strip grating on an amplifying substrate and their variation with laser settings.

articleTitle: Research of the Mechanism of Formation of a Pulsed Magnetic Field of High Intensity and Development of a Device for Therapy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The use of pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF) is considered a safe and effective method of treating various health problems. This method has been successfully used to promote fracture healing, alleviate mental depression, and reduce chronic pain and inflammation that are common in today's society. Currently, clinical experiments are being conducted in the world in order to better understand the mechanisms of its action and to determine the optimal parameters of use in specific pathologies, including acceleration of wound healing. The schematic model of the inductor operation has been studied, and its parameters have been determined. The proposed block diagram of the PEMF therapy device and the technical parameters of the device under development have been given. A device that meets the requirements for a PEMF therapy device has been developed and manufactured. The device can work in six modes of operation and generate paired bipolar magnetic pulses with an amplitude in the range from 0.2 to 1.2 T. Developed software allows setting the time of the treatment procedure. The device has passed clinical tests and has received a certificate of conformity as a device for medical purposes.

articleTitle: Subsurface and Remote Sensing Stand Development Using AD8302 Gain and Phase Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The laboratory stand was developed and tested for subsurface and remote sensing research using modern microwave components and AD8302 phase detector. The schematic diagram of the stand was described and presented. Appropriate radargrams were obtained for the cases of tested object buried in the dry sand and located on its surface in the laboratory conditions. The results will be used in future works to realize different measurement techniques for detecting landmines and improvised explosive devices at the base of different electromagnetic sensors installed in the unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Effect of the Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes on Dilatometric and Optical Properties of the Micro/Nano-Sized Cellulose
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The concentration set of the composites, where the micro/nano crystalline cellulose (M/NC) was used as a matrix, while multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) were used as fillers, were prepared and studied. The dilatometric properties (relative linear thermal expansion, coefficient of the thermal expansion (CTE)), diffuse reflection spectra, photoluminescence spectra and luminescence intensity have been measured and analyzed. The band gap Eg was evaluated, so it was found that Eg value decreases (3.6 →3.4 eV) when the MWCNT content increases. The temperature behaviors of the relative expansion and CTE revealed two temperature ranges with different values of CTE. Noted ranges correspond to parts of the cellulose matrix with various amorphous phase structures. Nanocomposite materials under study are characterized by photoluminescence (PL), whose spectra range from soft ultraviolet to red light. The PL spectra of “pure” M/NC are formed by a complex band lying in the range 350 - 650 nm with peak position near 425 nm. When MWCNTs are incorporated into the cellulose matrix the PL intensity decreses and the spectral profile is deformed. Thus, the UV band (peak position near 330 nm) becomes the most intensive in the spectra. An appearance of the and increasing its relative intensity is considered as features of the micro/nanosized carbon fragments/clusters/dots luminescence in the cellulose matrix. Concentration dependences of the intensity and of luminescence spectra confirmed the conclusion about the selective interaction of the carbon filler with different phase components of the cellulose matrix.

articleTitle: Modulating the Electronic States of Black Phosphorene as a Promising Material for Flexible Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The investigation revolves around evaluating how uniaxial tensile and shear strains impact the band gap within the electronic structure of monolayer black phosphorus, known as phosphorene. Employing numerical techniques to explore the band gap's response to different types and strengths of deformation, we utilize two methodologies. In one approach, the tight-binding model scrutinizes the strain-induced dependencies of hopping energies on bond length. Simultaneously, the second approach involves first-principles simulations based on density functional theory. Both methods confirm that phosphorene, initially characterized as a direct semiconductor under unstrained conditions, can transit into a semimetal with a closed gap under the specific deformation scenarios. However, the critical values for this semiconductor-semimetal transition differ depending on the chosen approximations and model parameters. The primary emphasis is on clarifying how various types of deformations affect the electronic properties of phosphorene, considering it as a promising material for applications in flexible electronics.

articleTitle: Q-Factor of Biconical and Bipyramidal Metallic Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The optical properties of metallic biconical and bipyramidal nanoparticles are studied in the work. The relations for the diagonal components of Q-factor tensor for biconical and bipyramidal nanoparticles at the arbitrary relation between their heights and the diameter of the base have been obtained in the frameworks of the equivalent spheroids approaches. The closeness of the numerical results for bicones and bipyramids, the base of which is regular pentagon, has been established, which makes it possible to replace bipyramidal particle with biconic one under the study of the optical properties

articleTitle: Nanocomposite Polymer Electrolyte Materials Based on Polyether, LiBF4 and Nanofibers for Renewable Electrochemical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Nanocomposite polymer electrolytes are promising materials for the manufacture of modern renewable electrochemical devices. The development and improvement of the properties of such materials is an urgent task today. The methods of differential scanning calorimetry and impedance spectroscopy were used for studying the thermophysical and electrical properties of the developed nanocomposite polymer electrolytes. Polyelectrolytes were based on polyether, nanofibers and lithium tetrafluoroborate. The analysis of thermophysical data showed that the melting point and crystallinity of the studied polymer electrolytes decrease with increasing salt content. The addition of nanofibers to the composition of the system further reduces the melting point and crystallinity due to the formation of a gel network. At 20% salt content, polyelectrolyte systems are completely amorphized, which is explained by the formation of electrostatic complexes between cations and ether oxygens of the polymer macromolecules. Analysis within the framework of the classical theory of polymer solutions showed that PEG has a better dissolving capacity than the PEG-nanofiber system, due to its lower molecular weight and the absence of a gel-like network. Values for entropy, enthalpy and Gibbs's energy of solvation were obtained. The analysis of these parameters showed that dissolution occurs spontaneously in the polyether-salt system. The higher Gibbs energy values for the PEG-nanofiber-salt system indicate that the gel-like network of nanofibers hinders the processes of salt dissolution, therefore, it is likely to reduce the mobility of charges inside the polymer matrix.

articleTitle: An SSA-Based Strategy for Extraction of Cardiac Sounds from Composite Auscultation Records
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The respiratory and cardiac sounds superimposed in the auscultation records are separated by Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA). It is based on the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of a trajectory matrix with rows formed of the fragments with the sequential offset of the record counts. The correlation properties of the signal determine the generated functional expansion basis. The obtained modes are sorted by their correlation with the initial signal. This procedure provides a proper selection of the most relevant modes. For a broadband signal, SSA acts as an adaptive filter effectively separating the frequency bands of dominance of cardiac or respiratory components. The low-correlated high- frequency modes are considered noise, and filtration improves the signal quality for its audio perception. The low-frequency modes that usually contain the most energy may sometimes be too noisy to reflect the intrinsic signal rhythms. In these cases, we advise filtering them first, to proceed with the successful separation of cardiac and respiratory components.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Hofmann-Like Iron(II) Spin-Crossover Compound
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: X-ray diffraction, high-resolution Raman scattering spectroscopy, and comprehensive physical property measurements were used to study the crystal structure, molecular bond composition, and magnetic changes of the PtpyS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Me mono-crystal composite. The PtpyS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Me was prepared by sodium hydroxide, 4-mercaptopyridine, and methylmethanethiosulfonate as raw materials, extracted by dichloromethane, and toluene and ethyl acetate as eluents. According to X-ray diffraction data, the specimen is a single- phase with a well-developed crystal structure. According to Raman spectroscopy, the types of chemical bonds in polymers were analyzed, demonstrating different types of vibrations of C- H and ligands. Additionally, the PtpyS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Me sample exhibits the magnetic spin transition during the heating and cooling process, indicating the existence of high-spin and low-spin states.

articleTitle: Refining Clarity Medical Image via U-Net with Tailored Architectural Modifications and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Development, implementation, and quality assessment of an augmented neural network with transfer learning methodologies, with a specific focus on denoising medical images are presented. The principal aim of research is to elevate the quality and dependability of medical images in conditions of limited initial data. The described method is based on the use of the improved U-Net architecture and is intended for well-established operation in the field of biomedical image segmentation, configured for the nuanced task of eliminating image noise.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistance Oscillations in GMR/TMR Structures Based on Canted Antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) can play a crucial role in several promising applications such as magnetic storage, medical imaging, sensor technologies, neuromorphic computing etc. Many of these applications imply the use of magnetic resonance in thin antiferromagnetic (AFM) films, which, being insensitive to dc magnetic field perturbations and exhibiting ultrafast dynamics (with frequencies of about 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{THz}$</tex>, envisions a number of perspective devices such as generators, detectors, scanners, radars, modulators, and others. One of the common approaches to investigate and develop these devices is based on the known spin Hall geometry and the use of AFM spin Hall oscillators. At the same time, the operating frequencies of AFM SHOs cover a comparatively narrow sub-terahertz gap ranging from 0.1 THz to 1 THz. In this paper we propose to overcome this difficulty (at least, partially) by using a magneto resistance structure (MRS) consisting of two layers of canted AFMs, and a nonmagnetic (metallic or dielectric) spacer between them. By numerically solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for each AFMs canted due to the Dzyaloshinskii-Moria interaction, we show that, depending on the operating regime and the spacer material, the considered MRS could have low and high frequency responses in the microwave <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim 70$</tex> GHz) and terahertz (F <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1$</tex> THz) bands, respectively. We believe that the obtained results are important for the development and improvement of spintronic devices based on AFM nanostructures.

articleTitle: Determination of Spatial 3-D Distribution of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Acoustic Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The acoustic method of detecting unmanned aerial vehicles needs further improvement in view of the possibilities provided by modern information technologies. The development of this method can be carried out by means of hardware and software. The hardware and software complex designed for the study of acoustic radiation directional diagrams of unmanned aerial vehicles presented in 3D format is considered. Such a visualization of the results of experimental measurements is necessary to take into account the anisotropy of the unmanned aerial vehicles acoustic radiation when creating multi-position passive acoustic surveillance systems (acoustic posts), including the location of sound vibration receivers in the atmosphere at certain heights (specialized unmanned aerial vehicles, balloons, metesondes, etc.). This complex provides certain a priori information necessary for the improvement of stochastic algorithms for the detection of unmanned aerial vehicles acoustic radiation against the background of noise and non-noise interference.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Cumulant Detector of Noise Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A cumulant method for noise signals detecting against a background of noise interference is substantiated. The sensitivity of cumulant detectors of arbitrary orders has been studied. To check the reliability of detectors, the probabilities of correct detection of a signal with different parameters of the signal distribution and for different signal-to-interference ratios were obtained.

articleTitle: Impact of Sintering Duration on Microstructure and Free Volume of Spinel Ceramics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A comprehensive investigation into MgAl2O4 ceramics, intended for electronic sensor applications and sintered at 1400 °C for 2, 5 and 9 hours, was conducted through a synergistic application of analytical techniques. The combined methods employed included X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, Hg-porosimetry, and positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy, aiming to explore the phase composition, microstructure, and porosity of the ceramics. The results of the analysis revealed that the obtained ceramics exhibit a dual-phase composition and showcase a complex microstructure characterized by a branched arrangement of grains, grain boundaries, and pores. In relation to the sintering duration, it was observed that an increase in the duration led to a subtle fragmentation of free-volume defects within the ceramics. Intriguingly, despite this fragmentation, the nanoscale pores exhibited a decrease in size, while their overall quantity remained unchanged. This finding suggests a dynamic interrelation between sintering parameters and the evolution of defects and porosity in MgAhl2O4 ceramics, offering valuable insights for optimizing their performance in electronic sensor applications.

articleTitle: 3-D Electromagnetic Wave Scattering by Two Silver Nanoparticles in Optic Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A method is proposed to calculate the three-dimensional scattering of a plane electromagnetic (EM) wave by multiple nanoparticles in the optical band. The calculation method is based on the solution of a Müller integral equation set. Ellipsoidal nanoparticles with the permittivity of silver and different electrical sizes are considered. The model of two nanoparticles with a fixed distance between them is studied at different angles of incidence and polarization of the sounding wave. The calculation results for total scattering cross-section (TSCS), extinction cross-section (ECS) and absorption cross-section (ACS) were obtained. Results of comparison with similar results for a single nanoparticle are demonstrated. The obtained computer simulation data confirm the availability of resonance effects (surface plasmons) in the studied nanostructures.

articleTitle: Comparison of Three Methods of Estimation the Speech Transmission Index
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper, the results of a comparison of the accuracy of the speech transmission index estimates by the formant method, full and rapid variants of the formant-modulation method for the case of noise interference are presented. The dependences of the bias and standard deviation of the speech transmission index estimates on the duration of the test signal and on the signal-to-noise ratio were obtained. It is shown that for the case of noise interference, the formant method is the most accurate, the most economical in terms of measurement time, and the simplest for practical implementation. The rapid version of the formant-modulation method is noticeably 4–5 times inferior to the full version in terms of measurement accuracy and 10–30 times inferior to the formant method. In order to achieve an acceptable accuracy of assessment by the rapid formant-modulation method, it is necessary to use test signals with a duration of at least 16 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{s}$</tex>. In this case, the bias and standard deviation of the speech transmission index estimate do not exceed 0.03 and 0.014, respectively, in the range of values of the signal-to-noise ratio from minus 16 dB to plus 16 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Sensitivity of Refractometric Sensor for Level Measurement of Liquid Helium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This work investigated the possibility of increasing the sensitivity of a fiber optic refractometric sensor with an external hemispherical optical detection element, aimed to be used for measuring the level of liquid helium in various reservoirs. This application requires high sensitivity of the sensor to small changes in the refractive index close to unity, since the refractive index of gaseous and liquid helium differs by only 2.6%. Analysis and optimization of sensor parameters were carried out using numerical simulations based on the ray-tracing method. The achieved sensitivity of 7.5 dB to a change from the air to liquid helium of 7.5 dB is sufficient for a reliable measurement of liquid helium level in tanks and reservoirs.

articleTitle: Effective Dielectric Response of Dense Ferroelectric Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We measured the temperature dependences of the capacity and dielectric losses of the tape-casted dense ferroelectric composites consisting of 28 vol. % BaTi03 nanoparticles (average size 24 nm) in the polyvinyl butyral polymer and 35 vol. % BaTi03 microparticles (0.5-0.7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\upmu\mathrm{m})$</tex> dispersed in the ethyl-cellulose., as well as the ceramics made from the nanoparticles using the annealing at 1250°C. The composite films were covered with Ag electrodes and the measurements were performed in a wide frequency range. Using the Lichtenecker effective media approximation, we analysed the effective dielectric response of the dense ferroelectric composites. To establish the phase state of the nanoparticles, we analysed the static <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Ba NMR spectra of BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>nanoparticles in a wide temperature range from 200 to 400 K. Obtained results revealed that the ferroelectric properties of the nanoparticles contribute to the effective dielectric response of the composites in a significantly different way than predicted by the effective media model. This counterintuitive conclusion indicates on the strong crosstalk effects in the dense ferroelectric nanocomposites., which can be very promising for their applications in nanoelectronics and energy storage.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Analysis of EEG for Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper addresses the intricate challenge of classifying electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to distinguish between individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Normal controls. Autism Spectrum Disorder is a complex neurodevelopmental condition exhibiting a diverse array of symptoms across social communication, behavior, and cognition. The EEGNetv4 deep learning model is employed, trained on data from a limited cohort of 9 subjects. The study utilizes a Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation methodology to assess the model's generalization across a small and unbalanced dataset. Following the cross-validation process, the model exhibits varying accuracies across folds, emphasizing the heterogeneous nature of ASD. Notably, the highest cross-validation accuracy is achieved in fold #3, reaching 83.53%, showcasing the model's proficiency in certain subject-specific contexts. Subsequently, the model trained on fold #3 is selected for further testing, demonstrating a test set accuracy of 74.49% on EEG data from two additional subjects, one representing a Normal control and the other diagnosed with ASD. This research underscores the inherent challenges posed by the small and unbalanced dataset, highlighting the necessity for cautious interpretation of results. Moreover, the absence of EEG manual preprocessing with labeling by experts regarding EEG background activity and the presence of significant artifacts that were not eliminated by prior events rejection underscores the potential impact of signal quality on classification outcomes. Despite these challenges, the study provides insights into the feasibility of utilizing EEGNetv4 for ASD classification and calls for future research to address dataset limitations and enhance model robustness.

articleTitle: Green Synthesis Principles for Development of New Luminescent Materials Based on the ZnO Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This research aims to implementation green chemistry principles in the design, synthesis, and application of luminescent materials based on ZnO nanoparticles, with a focus on sustainability and reduced environmental impact. The synthesis of ZnO nanoparticles follows environmentally benign routes, utilizing non-toxic precursors and minimizing waste generation. Green solvents and mild reaction conditions are employed to enhance the sustainability of the process. The luminescent properties are tailored by controlling the size and morphology of ZnO nanoparticles through green synthesis techniques. The green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles in polymer media exhibit intensive luminescent in the visible range. Possible electronic transitions those are responsible for origin of this emission are discussed. The materials show a wide range of valuable properties and promise in applications in various technologies such as light-emitting diodes (LEDs), biological imaging, and environmental sensing. The use of green chemistry principles not only ensures the eco- friendliness of the synthesis but also contributes to the overall efficiency and performance of the luminescent materials.

articleTitle: The Electron Transfer Dynamics in InP at Strong Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The results of a study of the scattering rates of the main scattering mechanisms, low-field drift mobility of electrons in indium phosphide are presented. A set of initial modeling parameters has been proposed, which correspond to a satisfactory agreement with experimental results. The field- velocity characteristic for the static electric field mode is calculated. The influence of a pulsed strong electric field on the dynamics of the electron transfer process in indium phosphide was analyzed numerically. An estimate of the cutoff frequency of the material is given.

articleTitle: Code Converters Based on a Dynamic Optical RAM for Information System Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper, the authors propose a new dynamic optical RAM based on a fiber-optic line. This device significantly increases the speed of information flows by reducing the time required to operate the RAM by 10. The proposed optical RAM increases the productivity and efficiency of information exchange between slow and fast devices of information and communication systems without software costs, which reduces the probability of failure by two times with the same buffer memory capacity. The authors proposed variants of the practical application of the new dynamic optical RAM.
