On its basis, a shift register, a serial-to-parallel code converter, a parallel-to-serial code converter, and a TDM switch for information system facilities were created. The time characteristics of signals in code converters based on a dynamic optical RAM are presented.

articleTitle: Extended Classifier For The Photoplethysmographic Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The methods for filtering, peak analysis and segmentation of the photoplethysmographic signals and methods for unsupervised cluster analysis are considered. The support vector machine classifier is proposed using the automatically segmented waveforms for supervised learning. The four known morphological classes of pulse waves are extended with three intermediate classes to improve the model's flexibility. The feature selection problem is discussed. The use of statistical analysis of the pulse wave distribution across the morphological classes for cardiac activity monitoring is proposed.

articleTitle: Study of Adsorption of Porous Silicon to Methane and Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The study presented by the authors analysed the sensitivity of porous semiconductors to gases. The results showed that the addition of catalyst metals Ni and Pd to the porous layer significantly increased the sensitivity of PS-based structures to methane (CH4) and hydrogen (H2) molecules. Specifically, Ni nanoclusters were found to increase the sensitivity to CH4, while Pd increased the sensitivity to H2. The experimental structures are capable of detecting CH4 and H2 even in the presence of atmospheric air due to their lower minimum detection temperature in comparison to existing semiconductor sensors. The sensitivity of the Me/PS-Ni(Pd)/Si structures to H2 and NH4 was investigated, and the results showed a sensitivity of 1.67 to NH4 and 1.75 to H2.

articleTitle: Exploring Nanoscale Heat Transfer: Non-Equilibrium Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Effective Thermal Conductivity in Silicon Nanofilms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Using nonequilibrium molecular dynamics methods in the LAMMPS software, heat transfer in Si thin films was studied. The effective thermal conductivity of silicon nanofilms was investigated as a function of thickness, temperature, and temperature difference between two opposite film edges. The results obtained are in good agreement with the known studies conducted by other authors on similar films. The effective thermal conductivity increases with increasing film thickness, and the temperature dependence of the effective thermal conductivity of the sample under study decreases with increasing temperature. In a certain temperature range, the temperature difference between the film edges has little effect on the effective thermal conductivity.

articleTitle: Suppression of Additive Noise in the Biomedical Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The problem for useful signal restoring against the background of additive noise in complex cases arising during the processing of biomedical signals is considered. In particular, the possibility of effective suppression of harmonic interference concentrated in the loaded frequency band of the useful signal and suppression of random interference of a limited level with an unknown distribution law is being investigated. The results of experimental studies on model and real data are presented, confirming the effectiveness of the developed algorithms in solving current problems of practical medicine.

articleTitle: Operation of a Terahertz Signal Detector Based on an Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junction in the Presence of Low-Frequency Johnson-Nyquist Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this work, we extend our previous temperature-dependent model of the terahertz signal detector based on an antiferromagnetic tunnel junction and then use the updated model to analyze the noise properties of the detector in the presence of low-frequency Johnson-Nyquist noise. We show that cooling the detector to cryogenic temperatures (~ 4.2 K) results in a significant increase in its output dc voltage and signal-to-noise ratio. This effect is found to be frequency dependent; the maximum improvement in detector performance is reached at a certain frequency (~0.15 THz in our case) due to the interplay between the effect of temperature on the magnetic and electrical parameters of the junction and the matching between the detector and an external electrodynamic system. The developed formalism could be used for the optimization of terahertz signal detectors and other spintronic devices based on antiferromagnets.

articleTitle: The Concept of a Mobile X-Ray System with Tomosynthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: COVID-19 pandemic distinguished the problem of sensitivities lack of X-ray radiography and overexposure of the patients in computed tomography. The war in Ukraine induced the huge amount of shrapnel wounds. These types of injury have non-standard position in the body and lead to low efficiency of even digital radiography. In addition, there is a necessity of mobile devices, because they are used in Mobile Army Surgical Hospitals. To solve this problem the preliminary design and parameters of planned devices for digital X-ray tomosynthesis for diagnosis of chest organs as well as shrapnel wounds are substantiated.

articleTitle: Utilising Vibration Feedback in Robotic-Assisted Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A lack of tools suitable for robotic applications in assisted surgeries is an obstacle to fully autonomous operations. In applications such as orthopaedic surgeries, where physically demanding and repetitive tasks take place, utilising robot as a medium between the surgeon and the tool can increase precision of operations. To enable it, a few parameters must be measured from the tool, such as forces between the tool and the object it is in contact with, torque, presence of contact, or a close-to-contact condition. Development of such a tool that would be suitable/certified for medical use and compatible for robotic application is rather expensive. Therefore, this paper focuses on equipping an existing tool with a vibration feedback measuring device, to enable robust object detection by the robot. Combined with a neural network (NN) the device is capable of 99.2% accurate prediction of collision when the NN is pre-trained on samples with different material properties.

articleTitle: Investigation of Photoluminescence and Raman Emission of Porous Gallium Phosphide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This article presents a study of porous gallium phosphode (GaP) utilizing photoluminescence (PL) and Raman spectroscopy, followed by its synthesis by electrochemical etching. The investigation identifies a blue shift in the PL peak, indicative of quantum confinement phenomena, and spectral confirmation of structural integrity through Raman analysis. Deconvolution of the PL emission into Gaussian components further demarcates a complex defect structure. These results contribute significantly to the discussion on the impact of nanostructuring on semiconductor properties, providing a pathway to the refined application of GaP in optoelectronic device engineering.

articleTitle: Flexible Humidity Sensors Based on Carbonized Nanocellulose for Wearable Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In the work, the carbonized nanocellulose (NC) films were obtained by means of vacuum pyrolysis technique. The influence of carbonization on the structure, optical and humidity-sensitive properties of nanocellulose has been determined. The study of optical transparency showed that after pyrolysis good transparent NC films became completely opaque in the visible spectrum with deteriorated transparency in the IR region. The surface morphology of carbonized nanocellulose is noticeably smoothed, and its weight is decreased up to 70%. Capacitive humidity sensors were made from nanocellulose films in self-standing configuration. It was established that device sensitivity is decreased by 40% (to 0.051 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{RH}\%)^{-1}$</tex> ) after carbonization. At the same time, device speed is improved by three times (up to 110 s), which allowed such devices to be used as sensors of human breathing or wetting of human skin for wearable electronic applications.

articleTitle: Formation of Two Controlled Radiation Patterns for GNSS Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: To suppress interference such as jamming and spoofing, signals from the antenna elements of a small antenna array after analog-to-digital conversion, after divider are divided into two channels and, after passing through the elements in which the weighting coefficients are formed, they arrive at two adders. From the adders, the signals are transmitted to the monitoring and control module, in which weighting coefficients and control commands are generated. After suppressing or weakening the interference, the signals are transmitted to the navigation receiver to solve the navigation problem. In essence, the above construction represents two antenna arrays having one aperture. The task of the first array is to form zeros in the radiation pattern in the direction of arrival of the extraneous signal; the second array scans in space, determines the direction of arrival of the interfering signal and transmits this data to form the weighting coefficients of the first array. The results of modeling the process of interference suppression by a four-element antenna array from three directions are presented.

articleTitle: Pressure-Driven Magnetic Parameters in Inorganic Cobaltite Nanopowder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The structure, morphology, chemical composition, and integrated magnetic properties of the cobalt oxide La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\text{Sr}_{ 0.4}\text{CoO}_{3-\delta}$</tex> nanoparticles were investigated by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and high-pressure magnetic method. The La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\text{Sr}_{0.4}\text{CoO}_{3-\delta}$</tex> specimens have been obtained using the sol-gel method, where the initial product was heated and milled, and the nanoparticles were then annealed at 900 °C. High-pressure magnetic characterisation showed that La <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\mathrm{s}_{0.4}\text{CoO}_{3-\delta}$</tex> powders at atmospheric pressure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{P=10}^{\boldsymbol{5}}\ {\boldsymbol{Pa}})$</tex> have two characteristic Curie temperature values, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< T_{\mathrm{C}1} > =\boldsymbol{253}\mathbf{K}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< T_{\mathrm{C}2} > =175\mathrm{K}$</tex>, which correlate with small and big particle size. Under hydrostatic pressure, these two Curie temperature values increase to 268 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}$</tex> and 180 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}$</tex> respectively. The calculated Curie temperature-pressure dependence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< \mathrm{d}T\mathrm{c}/\mathrm{d}P >$</tex> slope for the size grains is close to linear at 130 K/kbar and 100 K/kbar, respectively.

articleTitle: Theoretical Approach to Describing the Kinetics of Diffusion in Multilayer Zeolite Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A theoretical model of the kinetics of diffusion in a multilayer zeolite medium with different porosity indices in its layers is proposed. Mathematical models of kinetics have been supplemented for the application of boundary conditions describing mass transfer at the boundaries of the layers of the sample under study. Calculations of time dependences were performed for the concentration of adsorbed particles in the free medium of a zeolite sample and inside nanopores. The calculation results show that the proposed theory well describes the diffusion processes in experimental zeolite samples.

articleTitle: Thermal and Microwave Properties of Thermostable Cyanate Ester Resin / Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This work presents the investigation of thermostable thin composite films based on Cyanate Ester Resin (CER) network as the base material and the Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes (MWCNTs) as a filler. During the study of the thermal stability of the CER/MWCNTs nanocomposites synthesized, it was found that the presence of carbon nanotubes dispersed in the polymer matrix in an amount of 0.01 and 0.10 wt.% slightly increased the resistance of these nanocomposites to thermal oxidative degradation (in air) compared to the pure CER network. This is due to a certain contribution of MWCNTs, which have very high thermal stability. The radio-absorbing properties of the resulting films of the CER/MWCNTs nanocomposites in the X-band were investigated. It has been shown that when adding nanotubes, the attenuation of the electromagnetic signal increases and there is a slight dispersion of the increase in the attenuation of the signal in the direction of increasing the frequency of the electromagnetic signal.

articleTitle: Scattering of the Field of Electron Beam by Two Graphene Strips Placed on the Same Plane at THz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We consider the scattering problem of the H- polarized field of the modulated time-harmonic plane electron beam by two graphene strips in the THz frequency range. The problem is reduced to the singular integral equation with additional conditions. Numerical solution is obtained by the Nystrom-type algorithm. Our solution is meshless and full-wave. Maxima of the scattering and absorption cross-sections are observed near the plasmon resonances. In the case of the shift of the electron beam relatively its central position, additional maxima appear, amplitude of which depends on the value of the shift. Thus, such a configuration can be used in the particle accelerators for the electron beam position sensing.

articleTitle: Smart Knife Tool For Cognitive Assistance In Robotic Surgeries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A novel smart knife with a built-in electromagnetic (EM) sensor is proposed for robotic surgeries to provide cognitive assistance in terms of contact, depth of cut, and potentially tissue type detection. The sensing mechanism exploits the di-electric properties of tissues as indicators of their type, including cancerous ones. Such a sensorized tool could significantly improve operational precision. Combined with a robot-agnostic software/hardware framework, it can open new frontiers towards the use of augmented reality technologies in surgeries.

articleTitle: Pre-Requisites for Mean Square Error Prediction in Better Portable Graphics Based Lossy Compression of Grayscale Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Digital images of a rather large size are often employed in medical practice and other applications. It is desired to compress them if transmission via communication channels and/or efficient storage is needed. Then, lossy compression is mostly applied and an appropriate quality of compressed images has to be provided. In this paper, we consider pre-requisites for predicting mean square error (MSE) in lossy image compression by better portable graphics (BPG) coder, which is often treated as possible substitution for JPEG. It is shown that MSE and, respectively, peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) are well controlled by a parameter Q used in the BPG-coder to vary its characteristics. However, MSE also depends on the characteristics of the image, which can be described using entropy. Thus, it is necessary to take into account the image characteristics when compressing an image. This study investigates how well the entropy can describe image characteristics, namely the image complexity for future MSE prediction for BPG-based lossy compression. It is proposed to use entropy for MSE prediction in the BPG-based lossy compression as a classification factor.

articleTitle: Variable-Structure Interval-Based Duffing Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper deals with the design of a variable-structure chaotic oscillator for path-planning applications of autonomous mobile vehicles. This oscillator is designed as a result of analysis of the generalized dynamical system. We use interval methods to model such a system and take into consideration its nonlinearities. Our approach offers to replace exactly defined system nonlinear functions with domains where these functions are localized. We define lower and upper boundaries for these domains by using piecewise linear functions. The usage of these functions allows us to rewrite initial nonlinear system equations into linear-like form with linear terms that are defined in some intervals and thus simplify the system model. Piecewise linearity of this model gives us the possibility to analyze the system features by using various control methods. Such a model can be used in both real and complex domains. The consideration of system dynamics in a complex domain allows us to increase the order of the considered system and define a set of operation modes to design a variable-structure system. We show the benefits of our approach by studying the Duffing pendulum and designing its base variable-structure system.

articleTitle: Advantages of Weak Signal Model for Analysis of Frequency-to-Spatial Dynamics in Distributed Fiber Raman Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The applicability of the weak signal model for the analysis of frequency-to-spatial dynamics of fiber Raman amplifier (FRA) implemented in standard single-mode fibers based on silica glass is proven in our work. The quantitative criterion is derived for the critical power of the Stokes signal and FRA gain must not exceed it in order to maintain the nominal operation mode without self-excitation. The analytical expression of the criterion is presented in the form of the upper limit of the signal power and it contains practical values of linear and nonlinear parameters of active fibers used for distributed amplification of optical radiation. The suitability of our model for the FRA analysis was verified by calculation in the experimental conditions of optical signals propagation along standard silica fibers G.652 and TrueWave RS. Both Raman gain profiles of these fibers are given in analytic form. The results of a comparative analysis of the distributed FRA parameters designed for operation in the telecommunication C-window and depending on the length of the G.652 and TrueWave RS active fibers are presented. Advantages of the analytical model over other techniques related to direct solutions of complex systems of differential equations are discussed.

articleTitle: Metamaterials for Microwave Absorption and Reflection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Metamaterials, intended for use in microwave and optical devices, usually are defined from the standpoint of electromagnetism, i.e., as composites with negative values of dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability. In addition to this, we describe the properties of microwave metamaterials, from aspect of materials science. It is stated that metamaterials are determined by negative values of dielectric and magnetic susceptibilities that reflects negative response of polarization and magnetization to the applied electromagnetic field. This concept in no way refutes the prevailing ideas, but significantly clarifies them. Some possibilities of metamaterials application as microwave protective materials are discussed, including the lateral reflection of radar beam by metasurface, as well as the electromagnetic adaptable camouflage.

articleTitle: Disposable Bend Sensors Based on Nanocellulose Composites for Muscle Activity Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Strain sensors based on nanocellulose (NC) and its composites with polyvinyl alcohol (NC-PVA) have been developed. NC suspension was synthesized using the TEMPO method from reed stalks. PVA aqueous solution was mixed with the NC suspension and dried in a thermochamber. Strain- sensitive film Cr/Ni was deposited using magnetron sputtering technique onto the surface of NC, PVA, NC-PVA, and also on the reference material of polyimide (PI). To evaluate the efficiency of the strain sensors the electrical characteristic under bending were studied. It has been demonstrated that the parameters of strain sensors are depended on the type of substrate. The maximum strain sensitivity of sensors (2.48) was observed for nanocellulose-based substrates. However, these sensors are slightly worse in terms of time drift and reversibility compared to sensors on other substrates. The potential application of such sensors for analyzing movements of upper and lower limbs, facial muscles, speech recognition, and handwriting recognition has been shown.

articleTitle: Fundamental Limitations in the Properties of Microwave Protective Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: At present, main difficulty in low-reflective protective microwave coatings development is to overcome the contradictory requirements: to provide broad frequency range when saving small thickness of coating. The work discusses some electromagnetic restrictions in low-reflective coating implementation; there are also some limitations due to fundamental properties of materials used in the microwave protective absorbers. In their development, some restrictions arise precisely because of materials specific properties. In this aspect, various mechanisms of electromagnetic waves propagation and absorption in different materials are considered. The microwave characteristics of dielectrics, semiconductors, metals, magnets and metamaterials are analyzed in order to select optimal materials for microwave protective composites.

articleTitle: Unusual Microwave Properties of Polyurethane Composite Films Filled with Carbon Mesomaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This work presents the preparation of thin composite films using polyurethane (PUR) as the base material and carbon nanoparticles (CNPs) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) as fillers. The radio-absorbing properties of the resulting films in the X-band were investigated. The microwave studies indicate that the thin film composites based on PUR with CNTs exhibit improved reflection and absorption of electromagnetic (EM) waves, while those with CNPs show reduced reflection and absorption of EM waves.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Beam Instability in Semiconductor Nanotubes with Dielectric Filling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We theoretically study the interaction of a tubular electron beam with a semiconductor nanotube with a dielectric filling placed in a coaxial constant magnetic field. The beam, moving outside the nanotube along its axis, is assumed to be monoenergetic and non-relativistic. We have constructed a theory of hydrodynamic instability in such an electrodynamic system taking into account the retardation effect for electromagnetic fields. We have demonstrated how the quantum properties of nanotube conductivity manifest themselves in the dispersion characteristics of the beam-excited waves and affect the instability increment. Exactly, as the number of magnetic flux quanta in the nanotube changes, the instability increment oscillates, akin in its physical nature to the Aharonov-Bohm effect.

articleTitle: Electrochemiluminescent Sensor System with Pulse Techniques Using for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The application of the pulse electrochemiluminescent method of analysis of liquids for the development of new types of chemical sensors is discussed. The analytical system design and its units are described that are important for the pulse ECL analyses. The examples of homogeneous and heterogeneous ECL composition based on tetraphenylborate (TPB) coreactant with pulse excitation are presented. The research shows that the pulsed ECL method employing polymer film modified electrodes allows detecting TPB ion in aqueous media at extremely low concentrations and has perspectives for high-sensitive detection of other substances. The new pulse homogeneous ECL detection technique and correspondent instrumentation has a high potential of practical application for bioassays.

articleTitle: Haptic Stimulation Reinforces the Effectiveness of Motor Learning in Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The effectiveness of learning is defined by the optimal level of brain activation. The use of haptic technology promotes learning by changing of activation level. Event-related or task-induced desynchronization (ERD) reflects the evoked cortical activation associated with both sensory and cognitive processes relevant to the learning process. The purpose of the study was to analyze the effects of the haptic stimulation on motor learning and its reflection on the corresponding level of the electrical activity of the brain. The study was conducted on 20 male volunteers, aged 22 to 41 years. The learning was conducted in a VR simulator with the haptic suit (TeslaSuit, UK) as a source of tactile stimulation. Haptic stimulation reinforced the correct and incorrect actions of subjects during their training in virtual reality. To analyze the dynamics of brain activity associated with learning during haptic stimulation, the event-related desynchronization/synchronization method was used. We analyzed changes in the frontal areas (processes of memory and monitoring of the current state), sensorimotor cortex (control of motor activity), and parietal cortex (integration of information from most sensory systems). Event-related haptic stimulation accelerated the process of assimilation of new material in virtual reality, increased the average reaction rate and the number of successful actions, and reduced the number of unsuccessful actions when the test passed. The introduction of reinforcing, informing haptic stimulation into the learning process led to the activation of brain areas that are involved in the learning process, which significantly accelerated the assimilation of new material. An improvement in the planning of movements was indicated by the depression of the alpha rhythm, and an increase in the beta and gamma ranges. An increase in beta and gamma rhythms illustrated the activation of cognitive processes. The simultaneous decrease in alpha and increase in beta and gamma rhythms are markers of more effective learning. Subthreshold stimulation is marked by significant beta- and gamma-ERD of late latency (500–1000 ms) in the sensorimotor cortex, which may be associated with the processes of increasing the level of attention, processing input information, and correcting behavior. Threshold haptic stimuli elicited significant late latency beta-ERS (500 ms), which may reflect deactivation of the motor cortex after the cessation of movement. In the frontal cortex, theta-ERS (200 ms) after subthreshold stimulus indicates an increase in the level of vigilance. Gamma-ERD at 500 ms denotes strengthening the processing of input information. With threshold stimulation, beta-Erd(500 ms) may indicate a comparison of information about one's own actions and the haptic signal. In the parietal cortex theta-ERS at 200 ms after subthreshold stimuli indicate activation of the ascending attentional system. For the threshold stimulus, there is a significant difference in alpha ERD immediately and alpha ERS 1000 ms after the stimulus, which may reflect the integration of voluntary movements. The obtained results indicate a steady increase in the activation level under the haptic stimulation, which affected the effectiveness of learning.

articleTitle: Protein Biosensor Compared to Nucleic One
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Fragments of protein molecules are considered as sensitive elements of biosensors on surface plasmon resonance in the layered structure “prism - gold nanolayer - protein receptor”. On the basis of studies of protein molecules as possible channels of electron transfer through the ATP (adenosine triphosphate) synthesis system, their specific conductivity was found. It is an important characteristic for modeling the sensory effect, as it directly determines the dielectric constant. And the change in dielectric constant directly determines the sensory effect. It is shown that the sensory effect depends weakly on the length of the protein chain, except for a narrow region from 16 to 48 amino acid residues. At lengths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 16$</tex> amino acid residues, the conditions of surface plasmon resonance are not realized. In the region from 16 to 48 amino acid residues, the resonance wave-length increases rapidly from the near ultraviolet to the green range. When the number of amino acid residues exceeds 48, the wavelength of the plasmon resonance practically unchanged. Since natural proteins have much longer lengths, the change in the dielectric constant of protein receptors is largely unrelated to the change in their length. The effect of the refractive coefficient of the “input” prism on the resonance angle of incidence was also investigated. It is shown that preference should be given to prisms with large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim 2)$</tex> refractive coefficients.

articleTitle: Electrically Induced and Controlling Pyroelectricity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In natural and synthetic crystals, the pyroelectric effect is possible only in ten symmetry classes of crystals, but their technical capabilities are practically exhausted. Therefore, the quasi-pyroelectric effects obtained in the materials of other symmetries, which also have important applications in electronics, become relevant. These effects can be obtained in the layers of suitable materials by creating anisotropic mechanical conditions, as well as induced by an electric field applied to the paraelectrics and relaxor ferroelectrics. The work investigated physical mechanisms capable of causing a large thermoelectric response (similar to pyroelectricity) in the polar and non-polar structures. The analysis was carried out on the basis of Landau's thermodynamic theory and a number of simple models.

articleTitle: Detection of Erroneously Selected Cardiac Cycles Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This study describes the development of a model for detection erroneously identified cardiac cycles as a classification algorithm that is capable of differentiating the signal of QRS complexes from noise. To solve this task, about 8 public databases were analyzed. From these databases 13,712,521 normal cardiac cycles, as well as 678,641 cardiac cycles of various types were prepared. This amount of data was chosen to increase the generalization ability of the trained models and the ability to correctly work with cardiac cycles of various shapes and types. In this study 2 neural network architectures were developed - a fully connected and a deep recurrent neural network. The new loss function was proposed, which minimizes the false positive rate, that is, the probability of identifying a noisy signal as a QRS complex. This function also showed an improvement in the learning speed and also significantly reduced the problem of the algorithm falling into local minima. The deep convolutional neural network was able to achieve higher classification accuracy than the fully connected one. The classification accuracy of the convolutional neural network was 99% with a false positive rate of 1%. The trained models have been used to solve various tasks that require accurate determination of QRS complexes. Thus, the proposed models were able to improve the quality of detection of cardiac cycles by 5-70%, and were also able to improve the quality indicator for identifying low-amplitude late potentials by approximately 20%, reducing the dynamic time warping distance from 0.72 to 0.58 with a reference value of 0.52.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Variability in Normal Periods of Breathing in Sleep as a Marker of Obstructive Sleep Apnea Severity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the application of machine learning methods for the computerized apnea diagnosis and determining the severity of this disease based on HRV during normal breathing in sleep outside apnea episodes. Heart rhythm variability analysis is carried out using single-channel electrocardiogram signals. To investigate the potential of machine learning to identify patients with sleep apnea based on ECG derived HRV analysis, the publicly available Apnea-ECG database from PhysioNet was used, which contains annotations for each minute of recordings indicating the presence or absence of sleep apnea/hypopnea at the current time. The purpose of this work is to determine and compare the informative features of the presence of sleep apnea in patients based on heart rate variability indicators during normal breathing in sleep outside apnea episodes, as well as the selection of machine learning methods that provide the highest classification accuracy. The indicators of cardiorhythmograms in the time and frequency domains, as well as the sample entropy, were considered. Using different feature sets, classification accuracy was determined for binary (healthy controls and patients with apnea) and multitask (healthy controls, patients with mild, moderate, and severe apnea) classification problems with models based on k-nearest neighbors method, support vector machines, decision trees and ensemble learning. Using grid search the best estimators are proposed, which ensure the highest accuracy of classification: 93 % for binary and 86% for multiclass task.

articleTitle: Microscopic Basis of Dielectric Parameters Nonlinearity and Controllability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Manageability of electronic devices parameters are of significant scientific and practical interest. While electronic instrument making, a prominent place is occupied by various functional (smart) dielectrics, parameters of which can be controlled by electric field. Fundamental mechanisms of dielectric nonlinearity and the reasons of dielectric parameters controllability are considered. The nonlinearity of quasi-elastic polarization occurs, if under electric field influence the inter-atomic bonding weakens that increases the polarizability, while at thermally activated polarization decrease in concentration of oriented dipoles (or domains) in the electric field is seen so polarizability decreases. The controllability is due to a change in the rigidity of atoms bonding under electric field influence that reduces polarizability and all parameters determined by it. Another mechanism is a restriction in the freedom of reorientation of polar complexes or ferroelectric domains.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Control of Transformations on the Surface of Materials After the Electron Beam Pulse Treatment: Sub-Terahertz Ellipsometry Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the possibility of using sub-terahertz ellipsometry as an express method for the radiation-induced transformation diagnosis on rough surfaces of materials. The relatively large wavelength (2.14 mm) makes the ellipsometric method less sensitive to roughness and allows the study of the material properties. The principle and general scheme of the electron beam pulse treatment method are considered. With the help of terahertz ellipsometry, metals, alloys, metals with coatings obtained by micro-arc oxidation, and carbon plastics were studied. A conclusion is made about the possibilities of sub-terahertz ellipsometry for diagnostics of the surfaces of materials transformed by electron beam pulse processing.

articleTitle: Oxidation of Carbon Fibers: Effect on Their Microwave Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Carbon fibers (CFs) were prepared from viscose and oxidized with HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>solutions, which is an effective method for the carbon surface modification. The thermal stability of the oxidized CFs was investigated by thermal analysis methods. According to the results of thermogravimetric analysis and thermoprogrammed desorption mass spectrometry, the oxidized CFs contain carboxyl, lactone, anhydride, and phenolic surface groups. The relief of the oxidized CFs was examined by SEM. According to the SEM/EDX analysis, the oxygen content increases up to five times after oxidation. The used oxidation of CFs has a significant effect on their microwave properties in the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band. Oxidation causes a 4.3 dB decrease in electromagnetic wave reflection and an 18.3 dB increase in electromagnetic wave transmission. The studies show a correlation between the concentration of HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>and the reflection and transmission losses. This objective correlation suggests the possibility of programming the reflection and transmission loss values when modifying the microwave properties of carbon materials or carbon composites.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multichannel EEG Data and Heart Rate Variability for the Detection of Epileptic Seizures in Newborns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The article is devoted to the improvement of methods of analysis of multichannel signals of electrical activity of the brain and heart rate variability for the detection of epileptic seizures in newborns. The urgency of the problem is determined by the need to develop systems of non-invasive registration and analysis of biomedical signals for timely diagnosis of neurological disorders and prediction of epileptic seizures in newborns. Early detection of a predisposition to epileptic seizures is of primary importance in reducing the burden of the disease. This study is devoted to the application of machine learning methods to detection and prediction of epileptic seizures in newborns based on electroencephalogram (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV) parameters. The purpose of this study is to select the most important EEG and HRV features and the most relevant methods of machine learning for recognizing normal, preictal and ictal states in newborns. To solve the problem, EEG and HRV parameters were obtained in the time, frequency, and time-frequency domains. Using a model-based approach for feature selection, feature sets were selected showing the highest accuracy in the predictive models based on the k-nearest neighbors, support vector machines, decision trees, random forest classifier, and gradient boosting methods. The highest sensitivity to the preictal state was obtained when using gradient boosting - 99% with a specificity of 98%.

articleTitle: Stroke Rehabilitation Bracelet: Remote Monitoring and Real-Time Hand Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Stroke rehabilitation is a crucial pathway toward recovery, assisting individuals in regaining lost motor skills and promoting functional independence. The advent of wearable devices, along with advancements in artificial intelligence, holds the potential to improve the rehabilitation process. This paper reports on a novel smart bracelet designed for monitoring stroke rehabilitation activities. Its development, in collaboration with an expert from a rehabilitation hospital, ensures the device's clinical relevance. The device uses artificial intelligence to distinguish different daily hand activities, achieving an accuracy of 97% in differentiating between teeth brushing, hand washing, hand flexion/extension, holding the hand still, and random movements. A key feature of the bracelet prototype is its real-time monitoring capability, enabling healthcare professionals to assess the patients' rehabilitation progress remotely, while also allowing patients to monitor their own progress through a mobile application. Physicians can access historical analytics and personalized reports through a web application. The proposed device seeks to bridge the gap between in-clinic and home-based rehabilitation for stroke survivors.

articleTitle: Software Procedures for Training a Recognition System for The Differential Diagnosis of Patients Based on Diverse Symptom Complexes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper discusses the construction of probability density function models for parameter values in heterogeneous symptom complexes characterizing clinical cases of patients in their differential diagnosis with three possible diagnoses in the field of nephrology. The models are considered as a way to present practical experience of successful patient diagnosis and as informational support for making preferred diagnostic decisions. The subject of the work is the development of mathematical and software tools for modeling and using the obtained models in clinical case diagnostics. To construct the models, a database with descriptions of clinical cases by symptom complexes with eight quantitative parameters, annotated with confirmed diagnoses, is used. All available statistics of the database are transferred to the proposed step models, which differ in their properties from ordinary histograms and, unlike them, can provide unambiguous decision-making in the full ranges of parameter values in working windows defined by the database statistics. The relevance of the work lies in the fact that the mentioned probability density function models capture some characteristic aspects of successfully diagnosed types of symptom complexes and may add additional potential to the existing toolkit for diagnosing similar clinical cases. The content of the modeling method and its software implementation, as well as the voting criterion and the corresponding software procedure for selecting diagnoses by patient symptom complexes using the developed probability density function models, are discussed. The models and the procedures for their formation underwent initial statistical testing with estimates of sensitivity, specificity, and overall validity of decisions.

articleTitle: Microwave Properties of PVC Composite Films Filled with Ni0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4 Ferrite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This work presents the synthesis of ferrite with the composition Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>., its investigation by the methods of SEM., TG/DTA., PXRD., FTIR and the preparation of thin composite films using polyvinylchloride (PVC) as the base material and ferrite as fillers. Nickel-zinc ferrite nanopowder with a cubic spinel structure was synthesized by glycine-assisted sol-gel route. From TG/DTA experiment it was found that single phase product was formed already after combustion of dried glycine-nitrate gel. According to X-Ray diffraction and SEM it was determined that ferrospinel after annealing at 650°C during 5 h has a porous structure., homogeneous composition. The crystallite size was approximately 29–31 nm. On the FTIR spectra of oxide-polymer composites showed the presence of a characteristic band of PVC., ferrite and plasticizer. The radio-absorbing properties of the resulting films in the Ka-band were investigated. The microwave studies indicate that radio-transparent composite material was obtained on the basis of PVC/ Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>., with a weak dependence of the reflection value on the concentration of the ferrite filler.

articleTitle: Microwave Properties of Composite Films Based on Polyvinyl Chloride and Oxidized Activated Carbon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Activated Carbon (AC) prepared by the carbonization of pit stones was used as is and was subjected to surface oxidation with nitric acid (HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) to be used as carbon filler for polyvinyl chloride (PVC) in order to prepare PVC-based composite films. Thermal analysis of AC and AC-HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> revealed the presence of carboxyl, lactone, anhydride, and phenolic groups on the surface of the oxidized AC. The morphological changes for oxidized ACs were imaged by scanning electron microscopy. Microanalysis data showed that treatment with HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> increased the oxygen content by up to 15 wt%. In the study, we used X-band microwave frequency analysis to investigate the effect of AC-HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in PVC composite films on the electromagnetic properties. The reflection loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of electromagnetic waves increases with the AC-HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> content in PVC-based composites according to a linear law. High concentrations of the AC filler weaken the radio-masking properties of the investigated PVC/AC-HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>composites while improving the EM wave absorption capability.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Possibility to Provide the Capacitive Moisture Sensing, Invariant to the Composition of a Bulk Substance or Dispresive Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 42nd International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Different physicochemical composition of the dehydrated substances makes capacitive moisture meters sensitive to the ‘type uncertainty’. Traditional ways of the ‘type uncertainty’ compensation are effective when we know the composition of the substance and stop working when the composition is unpredictable. The solution is to use dedicated testing influences on the moist substance. Firstly, we have to measure the dielectric permittivity of the initial sample. Then, we have to perform two injections of moisture (testing influences). It helps to receive three transfer functions for the moisture meter, invariant to the type of moist substance but strongly nonlinear. The method of linearization, together with the substitution of direct water additives with another procedure equivalent to the real physical model of a humid substance, was investigated. It can be concluded that the method of linearization provided close to the linear equivalent of three transfer functions, which were strongly nonlinear. The procedure of simulating the direct water additives into a humid substance with metallic flat plates of different widths provided a partial solution, more suitable for water in oil (water-fuel) emulsions than humid bulks.
